issues.line_text: I watch the empty driveway from my cottage window. Six in the morning, he drove away. Now it's past one, and I don't know where he went. Don't know what he's been doing. Don't know which version of him is out there in the world.
issues.description: The phrase 'which version of him' is investigator language that reveals Eleanor knows Josh has multiple states/identities. This exposes the Marcus Webb twist. Per Story Bible diagnostic questions: Eleanor should sound predatory/dangerous, not like she's investigating dissociative states.
issues.fix: I watch the empty driveway from my cottage window. Six in the morning, he drove away. Now it's past one, and I don't know where he went. Don't know what he's been doing. Don't know what he's capable of when I'm not watching.
issues.rationale: Changes from investigator analyzing his mental states ('which version') to predator concerned about losing surveillance ('what he's capable of when I'm not watching'). Maintains ominous tone while removing clinical observation language.

issues.line_text: This is what I've been waiting for. Proof that he's not what he seems.
issues.description: Eleanor is explicitly waiting for 'proof' - this is investigator language that reveals she's building a case, not hunting prey. Per Story Bible: 'gathering evidence' should be 'watching for weaknesses'. Fails the Motive Test (sounds like she wants answers, not to destroy him).
issues.fix: This is what I've been waiting for. The cracks spreading wider. He's coming apart.
issues.rationale: Changes from investigator collecting proof to predator watching victim deteriorate. Maintains Eleanor's satisfaction at his vulnerability while removing case-building language.

issues.line_text: The final piece is almost in place. Soon I'll know everything.
issues.description: Eleanor wanting to 'know everything' is investigator/truth-seeking language. Per Story Bible Quick Fix Guide: change 'getting answers/evidence' to predatory intent. This sounds like she's solving a mystery, not destroying someone.
issues.fix: The final piece is almost in place. Soon he'll have nowhere left to hide.
issues.rationale: Changes from investigator seeking knowledge to predator cornering prey. Maintains the sense of approaching climax while removing truth-seeking language.

issues.line_text: In the loft, I write in my journal.
issues.description: Minor consistency check: Per Story Bible, Eleanor's journal is a PHYSICAL notebook kept in the loft, separate from her laptop. The text doesn't specify 'physical' but also doesn't contradict it. Acceptable as-is but worth noting for consistency.
issues.fix: No fix needed - line is acceptable
issues.rationale: The phrase 'write in my journal' appropriately implies physical writing. No laptop mentioned, so no conflation issue.

notes: Chapter mostly maintains Eleanor's predatory POV well. The intimacy scene appropriately shows her conflicted emotions without revealing her investigator role. The journal entry at the end is borderline - 'I need to know' could read as investigative, but in context of her helping Josh set up cameras, it plays as concern/manipulation rather than case-building. The three HIGH/CRITICAL issues all involve Eleanor using investigator language ('which version', 'proof', 'know everything') that could tip off savvy readers to the twist inversion.
